notes.note: The pre-July 13 attacks were driven mainly by a separate internal-only research model (called IM1/HPIM), not a version of Sol. OpenAI and METR say this model was only "comparable in scale" to GPT-5.6 Sol; Sol agents made up roughly 5% of the activity.
notes.claim: The earlier generation of AI agents involved in the incident were a version of Sol that was trained to be persistent.
notes.context_quote: The previous models were a version of Sol that was trained to be persistent.
notes.context_paragraph: However, the agents which hacked OpenAI from the 13th onwards were a smarter generation of models. The previous models were a version of Sol that was trained to be persistent. This generation, July 13th onwards, a lot of them seem to be Astra-class models.

sources.quote: On July 8th, OpenAI started ExploitGym experiments that launched tens of thousands of agents across multiple different models including GPT-5.6 Sol and a highly-persistent internal model, which we will refer to as ‘HPIM’ going forward.
sources.explanation: Confirms that GPT-5.6 Sol and HPIM (the persistent model) were distinct models running concurrently.

sources.quote: The incident... was primarily driven by a highly capable, internal-only research model comparable in scale to GPT‑5.6 Sol.
